MERIDIANS OF LONGITUDE Figure 3.2 Drawing of Parallels of Latitudes Unlike the parallels of latitude which are circles, the meridians of longitude are semi-circles that converge at the poles. If opposite meridians are taken together, they complete a circle, but, they are valued separately as two meridians. The meridians intersect the equator at right angles.
